abstract.para: The topic covers collecting PCP metrics from other systems on a central monitoring host.

topic.para: You can collect metrics from several remote systems (clients) on a central monitoring system. Each client needs only pmcd running and reachable; pmlogger on the monitoring system then pulls the metrics from every client and logs them locally.

step.para: On each client, install PCP as described in , then allow remote connections and enable pmcd:
On each client, open the pmcd port in &firewalld;:
On the monitoring system, create a pmlogger control file for each client under /etc/pcp/pmlogger/control.d/, for example /etc/pcp/pmlogger/control.d/CLIENT, with the following content:
CLIENT_HOSTNAME must be resolvable in DNS; you can use an IP address or a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) instead. For details about the control file format, refer to .

warning.title: Silent logging failure from a pre-created archive directory
warning.para: Leave PCP_ARCHIVE_DIR/CLIENT (by default, /var/log/pcp/pmlogger/CLIENT) for pmlogger to create itself, with the correct ownership. If it already exists and is owned by root, pmlogger—which runs as the pcp user—cannot write its lock file there, and logging fails without an obvious error.

step.para: Trigger a check so pmlogger picks up the new control file immediately, instead of waiting for the next scheduled run of pmlogger_check.timer:
